beats.summary: Michael introduces a charity auction called crime-aid to fight poverty.

evidence.snippet: Michael: To recoup their losses, I am planning a little charity auction, where people from all over Scranton can come and bid on our goods and services.

beats.summary: Oscar questions the value of the auction, expressing skepticism about spending money on unwanted items.

evidence.snippet: Oscar: So, in order to recoup the value of items we liked, we have to spend more money on things we don't want.
Who would ever come to this?

beats.summary: Holly scores the big ticket item, Springsteen tickets, which Michael considers a highlight.

evidence.snippet: Holly: Michael scored the big ticket item. Springsteen tickets!
Michael: Yeah, I think that's pretty boss.

beats.summary: Michael makes a humorous comment about the auction gavel and his bidding.

evidence.snippet: Michael: It squeaks when you bang it, that's what she said.

beats.summary: Darryl mentions a list of Springsteen songs, including some unexpected choices.

evidence.snippet: Darryl: Mike gave me a list of his top ten Springsteen songs. Three of them were Huey Lewis and the News.
One was Tracy Chapman, Fast Car. And my personal favorite, Short People.

beats.summary: David Wallace offers a weekend at his Martha's Vineyard house for auction.
